title: Lithic Orchard retail outreach jot
content:
One-page scratchpad for Lithic Orchard retail outreach (notes to self).

Quick snapshot:
- Company: Lithic Orchard (regional retail chain, 120 stores, e-comm + POS).
- Why they matter: modern POS + loyalty stack, strong digital roadmap; reported 40% YoY ecom growth last quarter. Potential first-mover pilot for embedded LLM-driven in-store assistant + returns automation.
- Where Redwood fits: latency-sensitive in-store use (edge/hosted mix), private deployment for PII in receipts, cost controls for high token volumes. Pitch: predictable throughput (Dedicated) + quick PoC via Hosted API + optional Private for compliance.

Account research notes (rapid, unverified):
- HQ: Portland, OR; CTO: Marcus Liu (eng org head).
- Head of Digital: Clara Montoya (driving checkout/returns automation).
- Tech stack: React frontends, Node microservices, PostgreSQL, data platform on AWS. Using Braze for marketing, Segment for tracking.
- Recent initiatives: 1) reduce cart abandonment on mobile 2) shorten in-store support time for returns 3) pilot conversational experiences for product finders.
- Budget signals: multiple job postings for "payments platform" and "edge infra" — suggests mid-size infra budget; CFO comment in article about focusing on predictable OpEx vs CapEx this FY.

Key pain likely to resonate with (hypothesis):
- Support costs for returns/exchanges are high (agents + floor staff).
- Mobile/ecom chat is slow -> lost conversions.
- In-store kiosks need on-device/low-latency LLM capabilities (cache + batching matter).

Decision-maker map (target outreach list):
- Primary: Clara Montoya (Head of Digital) — owns checkout & CX pilots.
- Secondary: Marcus Liu (CTO) — infra & security signoff.
- Economic: VP Finance (name TBD) — pilot budget owner.
- Ops: Store Ops director (for in-store trials).

Initial hypothesis PoC (what to propose):
- 6-week pilot: in-store returns assistant + one-click exchange flow powered by embeddings + retrieval + small LLM for dialog.
- Scope: 5 pilot stores, kiosk + staff-assist tablet; integration via existing POS webhooks.
- Success metrics: avg handle time reduced by 35%, NPS lift for returns flows, 10% drop in return-related call center volume.
- Pricing ask: small fixed pilot fee + usage estimate; can start on Hosted with dedicated burst, recommend moving to Dedicated if sustained.

Outbound sequence (lean, 5-touch, personalized):
- Touch 1 (Email): short intro + 1-sentence value (reduce returns ops cost by X) + ask for 20-min discovery; attach one-pager.
  Subject: quick note on cutting returns handle time at Lithic Orchard
  Body: Hi Clara — saw Lithic Orchard's push on improving returns. We helped another retailer drop returns handle time ~30% with a lightweight pilot. 20 min next week to share a tailored pilot idea?

- Touch 2 (LinkedIn + Slack if in public channel): share a short stat + ask about current experiment.

- Touch 3 (Email with micro-case): include mini-case study (anonymous retailer) + high-level pilot timeline.

- Touch 4 (Call attempt + voicemail script): two-line voicemail: "Clara this is Samira at Redwood Inference — quick idea for shaving minutes off returns queues, email follow-up with proposal."

- Touch 5 (Breakup + value keep): Final email with an opt-in to a 15-min "what success looks like" call + link to calendar.

Email templates (drafts):
- Cold intro (short):
  Hi Clara — I’m Samira on the retail team at Redwood Inference. We help retailers run low-latency LLM features (in-store kiosks, staff assistants) without blowing up token spend. Would you be open to a short chat about a 6-week pilot we can run in 5 stores to cut returns handle time?
  Quick bullet on outcomes and one-line CTA.

- Follow-up with micro-case:
  Hi again — one retailer we worked with saw a 28% reduction in return transaction time after a small pilot. We used a hybrid approach (hosted API for dev, reserved dedicated pool for peak hours). If you’d like, I can share the 4-step integration plan.

Call script (discovery focus):
- Intro (30s) — who I am / why Redwood.
- Lead with problem: "What's your current returns handle time?"
- Explore data/process: ticket systems, POS constraints, where knowledge lives (KB, docs, product catalog).
- Security/compliance gate: "Do you have an internal requirement for data residency / encryption?"
- Close: propose a lightweight pilot; commit to timeline and one observed metric.

Objection handling (short + pragmatic):
- "We don't have budget" -> offer a paid pilot or co-funded pilot; emphasize speed to value and low engineering lift for initial integration; show optional usage cap.
- "Security / PII concerns" -> highlight Private deployment & KMS/HSM options; propose bringing SRE/security brief and an NDA + SoW focused on data flows.
- "Latency worries for in-store" -> explain Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, caching + prefix KV to reduce per-token latency; propose 1-week perf proof of concept.
- "Too experimental" -> suggest canary in single store, fallback to current flow, A/B measure.

Pricing anchors (mental model to test):
- Pilot fixed: $20k (5 stores, 6 weeks) + min usage.
- Scale estimate: Dedicated POOL (reserved) + usage banding; call out cost per active session (model dependent).
- Offer pricing that frames Redwood as cap-ex friendly -> predictable monthly for Dedicated.

Technical integration notes (dev-speak):
- API: REST/SDK for text generation + embeddings.
- Most likely flow: embeddings-based retrieval from product/returns KB -> small gen model for dialog -> action call (create exchange in POS).
- Data: receipts contain PII; prefer private deployment or strict redaction/ephemeral caching for hosted.
- Engineering ask from Lithic: webhook to ingest return events; ability to mount a small retrieval corpus (product SKUs, return policies, FAQs).

Open questions to confirm in discovery:
- Do they have an internal KB we can index? (Confluence, Zendesk, internal SQL)
- Who owns PCI scope signoff?
- Expected daily/peak session volumes for returns kiosks.
- Preferred pilot timeline & store selection criteria.

Next actions (to-do list - prioritized):
- [ ] Run quick org chart lookup on Marcus & Clara (LinkedIn + Glassdoor) — Ethan to help.
- [ ] Draft one-pager tailored to returns assistant (2 slides + 1-pager) — Priya to produce by Mon.
- [ ] Build rough cost estimate (pilot vs Dedicated) — Samira (me) to draft; ask infra for model cost assumptions.
- [ ] Slack intro to #accounts-lithic-orchard with one-liner + ask for intros.
- [ ] Schedule security pre-brief template for customers requiring PII handling.

Notes to self (scrappy):
- Try subject lines: "quick idea to cut returns handle time" / "pilot: returns assistant for Lithic Orchard".
- Keep first email under 80 words. Always end with a single CTA (20 min).
- If Clara unresponsive, escalate to Marcus with engineering angle (latency + infra cost predictability).
- When we get initial discovery, propose a 1-hr workshop with product + eng + ops to map data flows.

Reference snippets to paste into outreach:
- "Predictable, reservation-backed throughput for in-store assistants — avoid token bill surprises."
- "We run hybrid pilots: start hosted for speed, move to Dedicated/Private for compliance and steady-state economics."

Slack and comms:
- Post a brief in #accounts-lithic-orchard with link to this doc and ask for known contacts.
- If we win pilot, need a services quote template for installation + training.

End of scratchpad.
(Informal / raw — keep updating as I learn more.)
